title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: 1,300 drones hit Crimea bridge; Kyiv struck
preheader: Russia hit two Kyiv bridges; Trump leaves for Asia summit with Xi and Putin.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Tuesday, November 17, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 7 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Ukraine hits Crimea bridge in record drone attack as Russia strikes Kyiv
stories.why_important: Russia's defense ministry said Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia to Crimea for a second day. The ministry said Ukraine also launched 1,300 drones, the war's largest attack. Russian missiles hit two bridges in Kyiv, and the bridge attacks threaten a key Russian supply route. The drone barrage shows Ukraine can reach deep behind the front line.
stories.what_overlooked: Russian-installed officials said the bridge damage was minor. The strike's military effect may be smaller than its symbolic effect.
stories.prediction: Russia may repeat strikes on Kyiv bridges in the next 48 hours. That will show if it is opening a new campaign against transport links.

stories.story_title: China confirms Xi-Trump-Putin summit for Nov 19 with no fixed agenda
stories.why_important: China said the first three-way summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will be in Shenzhen on November 19. The meeting has no pre-agreed agenda, an unusual step for Beijing. It could reshape how the three nuclear powers handle Ukraine, trade and security.
stories.what_overlooked: The Financial Times reports no pre-agreed agenda for the meeting. Beijing usually insists on strict formal rules, so the format itself is a concession.
stories.prediction: Whether all three leaders appear together on November 19, rather than sending deputies, will show if the summit is real.

stories.story_title: US tightens AI chip export rules to curb China's remote access
stories.why_important: Washington will require licenses to export advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil. The rule aims to stop China from renting computer power from far away. It follows the Nvidia scandal over suspected Chinese intelligence ties and comes days before Trump meets Xi Jinping.
stories.what_overlooked: A State Department official said Washington would not restrict foreign tech firms in allied countries, so the rule's reach is still unclear.
stories.prediction: The first license denials or waivers for Singapore or Malaysia within 72 hours will show how strictly Washington enforces the rule.

quick_hits.text: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Brexit 'has not worked' and Britain will begin talks with the EU on closer ties.
A US federal judge struck down rules setting fixed terms for foreign student and journalist visas, calling them arbitrary and unlawful.
French unions called a nationwide strike for Tuesday over pay, with students expected to join five months before the presidential election.
SK Hynix is racing to finish the world's tallest chip plant in Yongin, South Korea, as AI demand strains global semiconductor supply.
Trump said he may meet North Korea's Kim Jong-un in China this week, raising the chance of new nuclear talks.
Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark announced a Rwanda hub for rejected asylum seekers, drawing UNHCR warnings.
Trump left Washington for a week-long Asia trip, starting with a Quad meeting in Manila on security and trade.

views.framing: Frames the strikes as reciprocal escalation, stressing Russian retaliation on Kyiv bridges after Ukraine's Crimea bridge attack.
views.quote: Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, shortly after Ukraine's air force warned of incoming missiles.

views.framing: Stresses Ukraine's responsibility for the Crimean Bridge strike during a record drone attack, citing Russian-installed officials.
views.quote: Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge again overnight on November 17, said Sergey Aksyonov, the Russia-installed head of Crimea.

perspective_grid.blindspot: US prosecutors delivered closing arguments in Huawei's theft and fraud trial in New York. A verdict could shape Huawei's global operations and US-China technology tensions.
